title: Middock Energy - Grid Pilot Onramp Scratchpad
content:
Purpose: capture raw notes from 2024-10-14 kickoff + follow-ups. This is a working scratchpad for technical requirements, immediate gotchas, quick triage items, and next-step owners. Not polished; use when prepping follow-up slides or handoffs to infra team.

Attendees (10/14 kickoff):
- Tom Ridley (Middock) - Head of Grid Software
- Leena Park (Middock) - Data/Telemetry Lead
- Marcus Huang (Middock) - Security/Network
- Ariana Patel (Redwood SE) - primary SE
- Rafael Gomez (Redwood Solutions Eng) - fallback/ops

High-level ask from Middock:
- Pilot: ingest streaming smart-meter telemetry -> realtime anomaly detection + natural-language incident generation for field ops.
- Hard SLO: 95th percentile response latency < 300ms for short reports (<= 128 tokens).
- Throughput: avg 120 reqs/sec during peak zone windows, burst to 500 for short windows.
- Data controls: regulated telemetry, must remain in customer's VPC for PII-sensitive fields (masked), require customer-managed KMS for key rotation.

Initial architecture options discussed:
1) Redwood Private (VPC) with dedicated capacity - preferred for data-residency/KMS needs.
2) Hybrid: edge gateway in customer network that strips PII, forward to hosted Redwood with shorter TTFB but more compliance risk. Middock leans to option 1.

Key technical constraints noted by Middock:
- Telemetry records are compact but frequent; many short prompts are prefix-similar (same device metadata repeated) -> good opportunity for prefix caching / KV re-use.
- Typical input sequence length after enrichment ~ 220 tokens; the summary output usually 40-80 tokens. Occasional long-chain diagnostic traces produce 800+ tokens. Need fallback strategy for long sequences.
- Some device models send binary-encoded payloads in a proprietary format; they want Redwood to support a small transform lambda to decode on ingress.
- Network egress restrictions: only TLS egress to allowed endpoints; we'll need to provide list for infra firewall rules.

Performance/Model considerations we sketched:
- Candidate models: small-medium open LLMs (Redwood-curated mid-size) for cost/latency; larger models only for complicated diagnostic traces.
- Quantized variants recommended for the dedicated pools to reduce memory footprint and increase packing. Discussed 4-bit static quantization + per-channel compensation.
- Batching: continuous batching with adaptive max-batch-size 64 likely OK; but ensure max latency cap per request (we can use time-slicing/batch-deadline).
- KV / prefix caching: set up a 30-minute cache for device metadata templates. Need cache key strategy: hash(device-id + firmware-version + template-version).

Security & Compliance notes:
- Customer-managed KMS required -> Redwood Private must integrate with their AWS KMS/HSM. Marcus to confirm key policies.
- Audit logs: they want >1 year retention for request metadata (not full PII content). We discussed sending audit events to a customer S3 bucket via private VPC endpoints.
- Data minimization: propose a pre-ingest transform that strips MAC/IP fields before storage. Leena to provide example payloads to verify transformation.

Immediate gotchas / red flags (needs follow-up):
- Long sequences (800+ tokens) will break the latency SLO if routed to bigger models without burst capacity. Action: define routing policy to offload long sequences to a non-latency-critical queue (async job) or to a larger Dedicated pool with higher cost.
- Bursty windows up to 500 RPS could exhaust a single dedicated pool if not sized; need autoscaling & burst buffer policy. Rafael to propose capacity numbers and cost estimate.
- Firewall and network policy restrictions may block Redwood management plane callbacks (rollouts, metrics hooks) unless explicit allowlist entries are added. Marcus to produce whitelist list by 10/21.

Concrete next steps (owner + ETA):
- Leena: drop 3 representative telemetry files (small, medium, long) to Confluence page and mark redacted fields. Due: 2024-10-18.
- Marcus: KMS policy snapshot and IP egress allowlist for pilot VPC. Due: 2024-10-21.
- Rafael: draft capacity plan (GPU types, initial nodes, autoscale margins), include cost estimate for 3-month pilot. Due: 2024-10-25.
- Ariana: produce minimal pilot runbook: ingress lambda spec, cache key spec, routing policy template, and 1-page SLO summary. Due: 2024-10-22.
- PM sync: schedule internal product/infra sync to review runbook and cost by 2024-10-28. (Owner: Priya Shah)

Pilot runbook sketch (rough):
- Ingest: edge collector -> optional transform lambda inside customer's VPC (python, small container) that decodes proprietary payload, strips PII, enriches with geo/zone metadata, then POSTs to Redwood Private endpoint.
- Model selection policy: if input_tokens <= 256 -> route to "mid-speed" quantized model in pool-A with max-batch-size 48 and deadline 120ms; if 256 < input_tokens <= 1024 -> route to pool-B (larger model) with async-fallback option; if >1024 -> send to batch-async pipeline and notify field ops later.
- Caching: prefix cache for device-template strings keyed by device-id+firmware; TTL 30m. On cache hit, reduce model input by 60-80% (estimate).
- Fallback: if pool-A latency > 400ms for 5m window -> auto-fallback to smaller model with degraded fidelity + immediate alert to ops channel.

SRE/infra questions for internal team (to add to RFC):
- Which GPU family to propose? H100 gives headroom for large traces but costy; A10/A30 or A100 spot-reserved might be optimal for mid-size model latencies. Rafael to include perf numbers from our bench.
- How to handle token accounting in aggregated telemetry flows? Need clear mapping of telemetry records -> tokens for billing/telemetry (we should simulate token counts from sample files).
- Observability hooks: must export per-request token breakdown, model-version, routing-policy, and cache-hit flag. Instrumentation point: add header X-Redwood-Cache-Hit to request logs.

Quick notes from 10/28 follow-up (short):
- Marcus confirmed KMS integration pattern OK; he will ask security to approve the cross-account key grant.
- Leena uploaded sample files (confluence link above) including one long trace (1.2k tokens). We tested local tokenization; avg tokens/record ~ 260.
- Rafael's draft capacity plan suggests starting with 6 x A100 (reserved) + 2 x A40 for burst workers; projected pilot cost ~$45k/month (pre-negotiation).

Loose ideas / trade-offs we debated (keep for later):
- Use streaming partial outputs for field ops so they can act earlier (reduce perceived latency) vs. wait for full summary to ensure coherence.
- Precompute templates for common anomaly reasons and only ask model to fill slots — huge token savings but reduces flexibility; trade-off needs evaluation with product team.

Action items for me (Ariana):
- Draft runbook (see above) and send to Priya + Rafael by 10/22.
- Assemble tokenization micro-bench using Leena's samples and share numbers in Confluence. Target: show median token count and 95th percentile. Due: 10/20.
- Coordinate pilot kickoff call (week of 11/4) once infra signoffs + capacity plan approved.

Random scratches / snippets to remember:
- Cache key example: sha256(device-id + firmware || template-v2)
- Header for logging: X-Redwood-Template-Version: v2
- Preliminary SLA wording: "99.5% availability for inference endpoint; 95th percentile latency <= 300ms for payload size <= 128 tokens" -> verify legal.

Notes for slide prep (one-pager):
- Problem: Too many false positives in current telemetry alerts.
- Opportunity: LLM-generated concise incident narratives -> faster field triage.
- Pilot scope: 3 grid zones, 6 weeks, limited dataset (redacted).
- Success metrics: 30% reduction in false positives; median time-to-action down by 25%; <300ms 95th pctl latency on small payloads.

End of scratchpad. Keep this file as the living capture for Middock onramp. When items bump to near-final, move to shared_drives/company/middock-pilot or product/confluence draft.
